messages:
Anya (Support): Customer 'NovaChat' reporting repeated 429s after a marketing push. They're on the free tier and say it started ~10:15 UTC. Asking if we can do a short-term lift so onboarding completes.

Anya (Support): Pasted their failing curl and response below so SREs can triage.

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"gpt-4o-mini\",\"input\":\"hello\"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 30
x-request-id: req_01G7abcdxyz
Retry-After: 30
```

Anya (Support): Customer attached app id `app_novachat` and timestamped req ids. They also said traffic spiked from three regions almost simultaneously.

Mike (SRE): Thanks — first glance shows typical account-level throttle. Can you confirm whether all of that traffic used the same API key? If yes, we usually see a single-key hot-spot causing concurrent limit exhaustion. I need the raw request counts per minute and per-key from the customer (or their request-ids). Also send any `x-client-id` they can add to requests for tagging.

Anya (Support): Asked customer to confirm key usage and to provide a 5‑minute window of access logs. They replied: "yes, single key used by multiple workers in Kubernetes; we scaled replicas from 3->30 during campaign."

Mike (SRE): That explains it. Free-tier defaults: 60 req/min and 4 concurrent requests per key (soft). If many workers share one key you'll hit concurrency or token-per-minute ceilings quickly. Two immediate mitigation steps: rotate the key and shard traffic across additional keys OR throttle workers (max concurrency per pod). Also implement exponential backoff on 429s.

Anya (Support): Customer asks if we can do a temporary lift while they migrate to paid tier.

Mike (SRE): We can allow a short promotional uplift but need Sales sign-off and Billing approval (to avoid unexpected cost). Uplift is a policy action (temporary override) that increases per-minute cap and concurrency for a bounded window. It does not change their plan permanently.

Jordan (Sales): I can provision a 72-hour "burst pass" for NovaChat that increases concurrency up to 20 concurrent reqs and raises the per-minute cap to 500 req/min. I need the customer's billing email + legal entity to attach the promo. I'll create ticket CS-4578 and add the uplift details.

Billing: We can apply a zero-dollar promotional uplift for 72h, but we need the account id and PO/email. After uplift ends, normal caps resume — if they want sustained capacity we should convert to a paid commit.

Mike (SRE): Before we enable the uplift please have the customer rotate the key and test with limited concurrency (start with 5 workers). Rotating will avoid the storm effect from long-lived keys and helps us fingerprint new traffic. Also ask them to include `x-client-id: novachat-front-1` on test requests so our logs can isolate it.

Anya (Support): I sent rotation instructions and a minimal repro harness (curl loop with headers). Customer rotated key, sharded traffic across 3 keys, and ran a controlled ramp. They also provided two example request ids: `req_01G7abcdxyz` and `req_01G7efghijk` for 10:16-10:18 UTC.

Mike (SRE): Verified both requests in logs. After key rotation + sharding we saw acceptance rates climb and `x-rate-limit-remaining` stop hitting 0. I requested a short retention log slice and added a note to our rate-limit dashboard.

Jordan (Sales): Uplift provisioned (CS-4578). I emailed customer: 72h promotion active, concurrency=20, per-minute=500. Asked them to confirm when they're stable or if they'd like a paid commit quote.

Anya (Support): Customer reports 429s stopped within 10 minutes after rotation + uplift. They thanked us and asked about longer-term options. I recommended Dedicated or Paid Reserved for predictable throughput and gave our pricing link: https://redwood.ai/pricing/dedicated.

Mike (SRE): Added postmortem checklist: 1) shard API keys across workers 2) enable client-level headers (`x-client-id`) 3) implement exponential backoff + jitter 4) consider batching small requests into single calls where possible. Link to runbook: /docs/runbooks/rate-limits.

Anya (Support): Closing thread after customer confirmed stable. Notes: promo uplift ticket CS-4578, logs attached, suggest follow-up call with Jordan for commit quote.

SupportBot: Ticket CS-4578 marked RESOLVED by Jordan. :white_check_mark:

Anya (Support): Quick internal note — avoid messaging the exact free-tier numeric caps publicly; refer customers to account page or ask support for exact values because caps can change per promotion. :thumbsup:
